subject: chemistry
pattern: Carries about 8-9 marks in the Karnataka 2nd PUC board paper: a 1-mark (Lucas reagent, Williamson synthesis, denatured alcohol), two or three 2-mark reasoning or named-reaction questions (acidity of phenol, Reimer-Tiemann, Kolbe), a 3-mark mechanism or cumene-process question and a 5-mark question on preparation or reactions of alcohols and phenols. Examiners expect reagents and conditions on every arrow, correct products (o- and p-) and the mechanism steps of dehydration.

questions.q: What is Lucas reagent? What is its use?
questions.answer: Lucas reagent is a mixture of concentrated HCl and anhydrous ZnCl$_2$. It is used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols: tertiary alcohols give turbidity immediately, secondary after about 5 minutes, and primary alcohols give no turbidity at room temperature.

questions.q: What is Williamson synthesis? Give the reaction for the preparation of ethoxyethane.
questions.answer: Williamson synthesis is the preparation of ethers by the reaction of an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide. C$_2$H$_5$ONa + C$_2$H$_5$Br → C$_2$H$_5$-O-C$_2$H$_5$ + NaBr. The reaction proceeds by SN2 mechanism.

questions.q: What is denatured alcohol? Why is ethanol denatured?
questions.answer: Commercial alcohol made unfit for drinking by adding poisonous substances like methanol, pyridine or copper sulphate (and a dye) is called denatured alcohol. It is done to prevent misuse of industrial alcohol for drinking, as it is available without liquor tax.

questions.q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol. Explain.
questions.answer: On losing a proton, phenol gives the phenoxide ion, which is stabilised by resonance as the negative charge is delocalised over the oxygen and the ortho and para carbons of the benzene ring. The ethoxide ion from ethanol has no resonance; its negative charge is localised on oxygen and is intensified by the +I effect of the ethyl group. Since the phenoxide ion is more stable than ethoxide, phenol is a stronger acid than ethanol.

questions.q: Boiling points of alcohols are higher than those of ethers and hydrocarbons of comparable molecular masses. Give reason.
questions.answer: Alcohols have an O-H group and form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other, so a large amount of energy is needed to separate the molecules. Ethers and hydrocarbons cannot form hydrogen bonds with themselves; ethers have only weak dipole-dipole forces and hydrocarbons only weak van der Waals forces. Hence alcohols boil at a higher temperature. Example: ethanol boils at 351 K while methoxymethane boils at 249 K.

questions.q: What is Reimer-Tiemann reaction? Give the equation.
questions.answer: Treatment of phenol with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide at 340 K, followed by hydrolysis of the intermediate with acid, introduces a -CHO group at the ortho position and gives salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde). C$_6$H$_5$OH + CHCl$_3$ + NaOH(aq) 340 K → o-HOC$_6$H$_4$CHO (salicylaldehyde) after acidification. The electrophile is dichlorocarbene (:CCl$_2$).

questions.q: What is Kolbe's reaction? Write the equation.
questions.answer: Sodium phenoxide, formed by treating phenol with NaOH, reacts with carbon dioxide at 400 K under 4-7 atm pressure; on acidification salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) is formed. C$_6$H$_5$OH + NaOH → C$_6$H$_5$ONa; C$_6$H$_5$ONa + CO$_2$ 400 K, 4-7 atm → sodium salicylate; sodium salicylate + H$^+$ → salicylic acid. Salicylic acid is used to prepare aspirin.

questions.q: Write the mechanism of acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol to ethene.
questions.answer: Ethanol is heated with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 443 K. Step 1: protonation of alcohol: CH$_3$CH$_2$-OH + H$^+$ → CH$_3$CH$_2$-O$^+$H$_2$ (ethyl oxonium ion). Step 2 (slow): the oxonium ion loses water to form the ethyl carbocation: CH$_3$CH$_2$-O$^+$H$_2$ → CH$_3$CH$_2$$^+$ + H$_2$O. Step 3: loss of a proton from the carbon adjacent to the carbocation gives ethene: CH$_3$CH$_2$$^+$ → CH$_2$=CH$_2$ + H$^+$. The acid is regenerated. At 413 K, with excess alcohol, ethoxyethane is formed instead.

questions.q: How is phenol manufactured from cumene? Give the equations.
questions.answer: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is made from benzene and propene using acid catalyst. Cumene is oxidised by air to cumene hydroperoxide. C$_6$H$_5$CH(CH$_3$)$_2$ + O$_2$ → C$_6$H$_5$C(CH$_3$)$_2$OOH. Cumene hydroperoxide is treated with dilute acid (H$_3$O$^+$), which gives phenol and acetone. C$_6$H$_5$C(CH$_3$)$_2$OOH + H$_2$O/H$^+$ → C$_6$H$_5$OH + CH$_3$COCH$_3$. Acetone is an important by-product of commercial value.

questions.q: How will you distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols using Lucas test? Explain the reason.
questions.answer: Alcohol is shaken with Lucas reagent (conc. HCl/anhyd. ZnCl$_2$). Tertiary alcohol (2-methylpropan-2-ol) gives the alkyl chloride at once, seen as turbidity immediately. Secondary alcohol (propan-2-ol) gives turbidity in about five minutes. Primary alcohol (ethanol) gives no turbidity at room temperature; it appears only on heating. The test depends on formation of insoluble alkyl chloride through carbocation, and carbocation stability is 3° > 2° > 1°, so the rate of reaction follows the same order.

questions.q: Explain the cleavage of ethers by HI with the examples (i) ethoxyethane (ii) methoxybenzene (anisole).
questions.answer: Ethers are cleaved by HI at high temperature. (i) Ethoxyethane with excess HI gives ethyl iodide: C$_2$H$_5$OC$_2$H$_5$ + HI → C$_2$H$_5$I + C$_2$H$_5$OH; C$_2$H$_5$OH + HI → C$_2$H$_5$I + H$_2$O. (ii) Anisole is cleaved at the O-CH$_3$ bond and not at the O-C$_6$H$_5$ bond, giving phenol and methyl iodide: C$_6$H$_5$OCH$_3$ + HI → C$_6$H$_5$OH + CH$_3$I. Reason: the C(aryl)-O bond has partial double bond character due to resonance and the sp$^2$ carbon holds the oxygen more strongly. Phenol does not react further to give halobenzene.

questions.q: Explain why Williamson synthesis fails with tertiary alkyl halides. Prepare 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane by a suitable method.
questions.answer: Williamson synthesis is an SN2 reaction. Alkoxides are strong bases; with tertiary alkyl halides, steric hindrance prevents SN2 attack and the alkoxide abstracts a proton, giving an alkene by elimination. Hence an ether with a tertiary alkyl group is made by taking the tertiary alkoxide and a primary halide: (CH$_3$)$_3$C-ONa + CH$_3$Br → (CH$_3$)$_3$C-O-CH$_3$ + NaBr (2-methoxy-2-methylpropane). The reverse combination, CH$_3$ONa + (CH$_3$)$_3$CBr, would give 2-methylpropene.

questions.q: Explain with equations any four methods of preparation of alcohols.
questions.answer: (1) Acid-catalysed hydration of alkenes (Markovnikov): CH$_3$CH=CH$_2$ + H$_2$O/H$^+$ → CH$_3$CH(OH)CH$_3$. (2) Hydroboration-oxidation (anti-Markovnikov): CH$_3$CH=CH$_2$ + B$_2$H$_6$ → (CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$)$_3$B; with H$_2$O$_2$/NaOH → CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$OH. (3) Grignard reagent with aldehydes/ketones, then hydrolysis: HCHO + RMgX gives primary alcohol; other aldehydes give secondary; ketones give tertiary alcohols. (4) Reduction of aldehydes and ketones with NaBH$_4$ or LiAlH$_4$ (or H$_2$/Ni) gives primary and secondary alcohols; carboxylic acids and esters are reduced to primary alcohols by LiAlH$_4$. (5) Hydrolysis of alkyl halide with aq. KOH gives alcohol.

questions.q: Explain the following reactions of phenol with equations: (i) bromination (ii) nitration (iii) reaction with zinc dust (iv) oxidation (v) reaction with sodium hydroxide.
questions.answer: (i) Bromine water gives a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol; in CS$_2$ at low temperature, o- and p-bromophenol form. (ii) Dilute HNO$_3$ at 298 K gives o- and p-nitrophenol (separated by steam distillation, o- is steam volatile due to intramolecular H-bonding); conc. HNO$_3$ gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid). (iii) Phenol distilled with zinc dust gives benzene: C$_6$H$_5$OH + Zn → C$_6$H$_6$ + ZnO. (iv) Oxidation with chromic acid gives benzoquinone (p-benzoquinone). (v) Phenol reacts with NaOH to give sodium phenoxide and water, showing its acidic nature: C$_6$H$_5$OH + NaOH → C$_6$H$_5$ONa + H$_2$O.

questions.q: Explain the following reactions of ethanol: (i) with sodium (ii) esterification with acetic acid (iii) oxidation with PCC and with acidified KMnO$_4$ (iv) dehydration at 413 K.
questions.answer: (i) With sodium, hydrogen is evolved showing acidic character: 2C$_2$H$_5$OH + 2Na → 2C$_2$H$_5$ONa + H$_2$. (ii) Esterification: C$_2$H$_5$OH + CH$_3$COOH, conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ (reversible) → CH$_3$COOC$_2$H$_5$ + H$_2$O (ethyl ethanoate). (iii) PCC in CH$_2$Cl$_2$ stops at the aldehyde: CH$_3$CH$_2$OH → CH$_3$CHO; acidified KMnO$_4$ or K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ oxidises further to ethanoic acid CH$_3$COOH. (iv) Dehydration with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 413 K with excess ethanol gives ethoxyethane: 2C$_2$H$_5$OH → C$_2$H$_5$OC$_2$H$_5$ + H$_2$O; at 443 K ethene is formed.
